title: prefix-load streaming: delta-KV stitching and kernel pacing hints for smoother handoff
author: Ethan Morales
release_notes: Introduces prefix-load streaming with delta-based KV writes and kernel pacing hints. Improves median latency and tail behavior for mixed short/long prompt workloads. Backwards-compatible via feature flag.
description:
Context & motivation:
We observed two correlated issues on mixed-length workloads: (1) redundant KV writes from eager full-prefill cause unnecessary memory churn and GPU work when requests abort or finish quickly, and (2) synchronous prefill->decode handoffs create spikey load patterns that force conservative kernel choices and increase tail latency. This PR introduces a different handoff model: "prefix-load streaming" where the prefill stage emits compact delta patches to the KV store and a lightweight progress signal to the scheduler; the decode stage consumes the streamed prefix and applies deltas on-the-fly while using admission-provided kernel-pacing hints to select kernels and batching strategy.

Design summary:
- Delta-KV stitcher: instead of writing a full KV snapshot at prefix completion, the prefill stage writes incremental deltas (key segments + sequence ranges) which the KV layer can stitch into existing entries atomically. This reduces write amplification and enables fast rollback for speculative prefetching.
- Signalless/compact handoff: handoff is intentionally low-bandwidth: a small progress token (sequence cursor + patch metadata) is used to coordinate stages. This token removes the need for heavy synchronization during common-case continuous streaming while still supporting robust consistency checks.
- Kernel pacing hints: the admission controller emits a short-lived hint describing intended decode pacing (e.g., latency-priority vs throughput-priority, expected average sequence length). Kernels expose a lightweight hint API to pick more appropriate execution paths (e.g., larger continuous-batched matmul vs single-step low-latency kernel).
- Safety & fallback: if the KV stitcher detects a mismatch (out-of-order deltas or missing baseline), it falls back to conservative full-rewrite semantics for that request. Kernel hint mismatch reverts to current kernel selection logic. The feature is gated behind a feature flag for safe rollout.

Implementation notes:
- serve/runtime/kv/delta_stitcher.cpp: new delta encoding, atomic apply path, and lightweight checksum to detect drift.
- serve/runtime/pipeline/prefix_stream.go: streaming API for prefill to emit deltas and progress tokens; includes backpressure window compression to avoid excessive token churn.
- serve/runtime/kernel/admission.go: hint emission logic integrated into the admission path, and mapping to kernel selectors.
- console/flags/feature_flags.go & docs/perf/prefix_load.md: feature flag + runbook and instrumentation notes.
- integration tests: pipeline_integration_test.py simulates mixed-length workload distribution and verifies KV consistency under simulated prefill aborts.

Performance & test results:
- Canary on a dedicated GPU pool (r4.2x) with 40/60 short/long mix: median latency improved ~9% for end-to-end generation; 95th percentile reduced by ~18%.
- GPU token work (measured via per-token matmul counters) decreased by ~7% on workloads with >=20% early-abort rate due to reduced KV rewrite amplification.
- Unit/integration test coverage added for delta application, rollback, and kernel hint mapping.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge gated behind feature flag default-off.
2) Enable on a single canary pool for 48 hours, collect tail-latency and KV-metrics.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% traffic with automatic rollback if KV inconsistency or >5% regression in median latency occurs.

Notes & related work:
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-1984 (KV write amplification investigation), ENG-2050 (kernel selection improvements).
- This approach intentionally avoids changing kernel implementations beyond a small hint API to reduce risk; future follow-ups may add richer kernel paths if signals justify it.
